title: The Ins and Outs of Albinism
summary: Josh and Chuck explain albinism: a genetic, autosomal recessive condition that reduces or eliminates melanin production, with the enzyme tyrosinase central to melanin synthesis. They cover types (oculocutaneous albinism, OCA1A through OCA types), the eye and vision effects such as photophobia and retinal damage, the link to neural crest development, and the lack of a cure. They discuss albinism in animals and plants (corn), melanin's role in bird and mammal coloration, social stigma and violence against people with albinism in parts of Africa, and the inheritance pattern through carriers. They also cover related conditions that are not albinism (vitiligo, poliosis, Waardenburg syndrome, piebald coloration). The episode closes with a listener mail correction about spelling and dyslexia.

segments.title: Opening and overview of albinism
segments.summary: The hosts introduce albinism, note preferred terminology (people with albinism rather than albinos), mention albinism in animals and plants, and give a broad overview of melanin's role, the eyes' red appearance, and the myth that red eyes are required for albinism.

segments.title: Corn, types of albinism, and sun and vision effects
segments.summary: The hosts discuss albinism in corn, the idea that albinism is not necessarily harmful by itself, and the syndromic and non-syndromic distinction. They mention the possible link between vision problems and autism, and describe albinism as a neural crest disorder with no treatment.

segments.title: Oculocutaneous albinism and eye effects
segments.summary: The hosts describe oculocutaneous albinism (OCA), the most common and most distinct form, and the subtypes OCA1A through others. They explain how lack of pigment causes light sensitivity, retinal damage, photophobia, and vision problems that affect school, along with stereotypes of albino villains in film.

segments.title: Social challenges, schooling, and stigma
segments.summary: The hosts discuss schooling and bullying experienced by people with albinism, and the value of educating children about differences. They then cover stigma and myths in parts of Africa, including the belief that albinism is contagious and the violence and body trade against people with albinism.

segments.title: Tyrosinase, melanin production, and inheritance
segments.summary: The hosts explain that tyrosinase is the key enzyme starting melanin production, and that a disruption early in the chain causes complete lack of pigment. They explain the autosomal recessive inheritance pattern, why two non-affected carriers can have an affected child, and how this differs across animals.

segments.title: Related pigment conditions
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish albinism from vitiligo (now thought to be autoimmune), poliosis (a patch of white hair, not related to polio), Waardenburg syndrome, and piebald coloration in horses and humans.

segments.title: Listener mail on spelling and dyslexia
segments.summary: A listener named Natalie, an adult with dyslexia, points out that the hosts implied poor spelling means lack of intelligence in an earlier episode. Josh and Chuck apologize and thank her. They also close the episode with a sign-off.
